chunks: And from him, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Abu al-Khattab, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him), who said:
I said to him: A man forgot to say the Takbir of Opening until he had already said Takbir for bowing (Ruku'). He said: 'It is sufficient for him.'

Therefore, these two hadiths are applied to one who forgot the Takbir of Opening and then did not become certain that he had not said it, but rather was in doubt; for in that case it is obligatory upon him to proceed in his prayer.
As for with certainty and knowledge that he did not say it, it is obligatory upon him to repeat the prayer, based on the indication of the reports we have previously mentioned.

Also, the report we mentioned from Ibn Abi Yafur and al-Fadl ibn Abd al-Malik from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) included explicit statement that the Takbir in Ruku' does not suffice for the Takbir of Opening, and that with knowledge, it is necessary to repeat the prayer.
So we know that what these two reports included regarding the permissibility of that is only in the case of doubt, not certainty.
And that which confirms what we mentioned, added to what we have previously mentioned, is what he narrated:

key_terms.تَكْبِيرَةُ الْافتِتَاحِ: Takbir of Opening (the initial declaration of greatness at the start of prayer)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if one forgets the opening Takbir during prayer?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi clarifies the apparent discrepancy in hadiths by distinguishing between doubt (shakk) and certainty (yaqin) regarding the missed Takbirat al-Iftitah. He establishes that while proceeding in prayer is sufficient for the doubter, certainty of omission necessitates prayer repetition, a ruling reinforced by the explicit statement that the bowing Takbir does not substitute for the opening one.
